question: Praveen Kumar, awarded the Khel Ratna, in January 2025, is associated with which discipline?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Para-Athletics**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Praveen Kumar** is an acclaimed Indian athlete associated with **Para-Athletics**, a discipline focused on athletes with physical disabilities.
 
• He was awarded the prestigious **Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award** (now renamed Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award) in **January 2025** for his outstanding achievements in Para-Athletics.
 
• Praveen Kumar has excelled in international Para-Athletics events, earning medals and recognition for India. His remarkable performance in events like **High Jump** has significantly contributed to India's recognition in this category.
 
• **Para-Athletics** includes track and field events modified for athletes with physical impairments, providing them a platform to showcase their sportsmanship on national and international levels.
 
• The award emphasizes the importance of recognizing achievements in **Para-Sports**, promoting inclusivity and encouraging athletes with disabilities to pursue their dreams in competitive sports.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Para-Athletics:**

 
 
• Para-Athletics is governed by the **International Paralympic Committee (IPC)**, which sets the rules and classification system for athletes with disabilities.
 
• It includes various events like **sprints, long-distance running, high jump, discus throw, javelin throw, and shot put**, tailored for athletes based on their physical capabilities.
 
• India has been actively participating in Para-Athletics events since its debut at the Paralympics in **1968**.
 
• Athletes are classified into different categories like **visual impairment, amputee, wheelchair-bound, and cerebral palsy** to ensure fair competition.
 
 
 
• **Khel Ratna Award:**
 
 
• Renamed as **Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award**, it is India's highest sporting honor.
 
• Instituted in **1991-92**, the award recognizes outstanding performance in sports across disciplines.
 
• Recipients are awarded a **medal, certificate, and a cash prize**. As of recent updates, the cash prize is **₹25 lakh**.
 
• Prominent athletes like **Sachin Tendulkar, PV Sindhu, and Neeraj Chopra** have been honored with this award.
 
 
 
• **Achievements of Praveen Kumar:**
 
 
• Praveen Kumar is renowned for his **High Jump** performances in Para-Athletics, especially in the **T64 category** for athletes with leg impairments.
 
• He won a **silver medal** at the **Tokyo Paralympics 2020**, setting an Asian record with a jump of **2.07 meters**.
 
• He has also bagged medals in other international events, showcasing exceptional consistency and dedication.
 
 
 
• **Importance of Para-Sports:**
 
 
• Para-Sports provide a platform for athletes with disabilities to excel and demonstrate their abilities.
 
• They promote **inclusivity, equality, and awareness** about the capabilities of differently-abled individuals.
 
• Events like the **Paralympics** and **World Para Athletics Championships** have gained significant global recognition, emphasizing the importance of these sports.
 
• India has been actively encouraging Para-Sports through schemes like the **Target Olympic Podium Scheme (TOPS)** and dedicated training facilities.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Prominent Para-Athletes in India:**

 
 
• **Devendra Jhajharia**: Two-time Paralympic Gold medalist in Javelin Throw.
 
• **Deepa Malik**: First Indian woman to win a medal at the Paralympics; achieved in Shot Put.
 
• **Mariyappan Thangavelu**: Gold medalist in High Jump at the Rio Paralympics 2016.
 
• Such athletes inspire millions and highlight the potential of Para-Sports in India.
 
 
 
• **Government Support:**
 
 
• India has launched initiatives like the **Para-Athlete Development Programme** and increased funding through the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports.
 
• Facilities like **specialized coaching, international exposure, and financial aid** are provided to athletes.
